title: Chinese scientists solve 30-year-old mathematical conjecture using a domestic AI model
key_facts: The Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory announced on 15 Oct 2026 that the three-dimensional Ghys conjecture has been solved.
Xu Disheng, visiting scholar at the lab and professor at Greater Bay Area University, led the team and used the lab's Shuwen-S2 multimodal model with human-machine collaboration.
A Peking University team (Professor Dong Bin and Academician Liu Ruochuan) used its SHEAF framework to verify the proof formally.
French mathematician Étienne Ghys proposed the conjecture in 1995.
The paper is on the arXiv preprint platform and the formal code is public on GitHub.
The lab says this is the first time Chinese scientists solved a world-class maths problem with a Chinese large model.
The lab plans to fold the verification module into its Shengwen Duanyan Scientific Discovery Platform.
quote_evidence: This marks the first time Chinese scientists have solved a world-class mathematical problem using a Chinese large model.
The related paper has been published on the preprint platform arXiv, and its formalized code is also publicly available on GitHub.
why_it_matters_hint: A claimed AI-assisted proof of a long-open problem, with a public computer-checkable record.
notes: KuCoin carries IT Home text; all claims are the lab's own. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
